answer: The strongest lever is simple: mix in randomly chosen human-authored live tasks that cannot be precomputed, because pulse only stays cheap while clones that dodge the live lane lose the epoch payout entirely. Concretely, jetty is enforced in the ledger: Reputation is transferable only on sale, so an attacker cannot resell a fully warmed clone cheaply. Any karst approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
